p: There are really two ways to enjoy this place, and both are worth a go. The first is the obvious one: book a public session, lace up and have a laugh. The second is to come back on a game night and watch the Hawks in action from the stands. Ice hockey is fast, loud and properly exciting to watch live, even if you don't know the rules. The puck moves so quickly that half the fun is trying to keep up with it, and the crowd noise in a rink this size is something else.

If you've never been to a hockey match, wrap up warm. Rinks are chilly even from the seats, and a coat, hat and gloves will keep you comfy through the periods. Kids tend to love the speed and the drama, which makes it a great family night out with a difference.

For a public skate, give yourself time at the start to get your hire boots fitted properly. Laces tight around the ankle, toes not squashed, heel snug in the back. It makes a huge difference to how steady you feel on the ice.

Blackburn has plenty to fill the rest of the day. Witton Country Park on the west side of town is a lovely green space with walks and play areas, and if you fancy a climb, Darwen Tower on the moors just south of town rewards you with big views across Lancashire. Blackburn Cathedral is right in the town centre for a calmer stop, and football fans won't need telling that Ewood Park, home of Blackburn Rovers, is part of the local landscape.
